newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Bangladesh urges U.S. to write off $800 mln debt.
newsitem.headline: Bangladesh urges U.S. to write off $800 mln debt.

text.p: Bangladesh Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina, now visiting the United States, urged Washington to write off $800 million that Dhaka received as food assistance, the official BSS news agency said on Thursday.

"I would strongly urge you to take steps to write off the food assistance," the agency quoted Hasina as telling a meeting with members of the House of Representatives Committee on International Relations in Washington on Wednesday.
In 1991, the U.S., one of Dhaka's major aid donors, had written off $300 million in debt to Bangladesh.

Hasina, who chaired the World Micro Credit Summit in Washington that ended on Tuesday, told the U.S. Congressmen that Bangladesh-U.S. relations were based on a "solid foundation" and had grown steadily both "in scope and depth".
Chairman of the committee, Benjamin Gilman, was present at the Capitol Hill meeting, BSS said without giving further details.
